summary: This is a measurement-only repair of the 2026-07-20 email-gate diagnostic, and it is honest, well-evidenced, and correctly scoped: every number, command, and code-line the planner cites reproduces exactly, the assumed cause is a code-level certainty rather than a statistical guess, and it touches nothing a visitor sees, gives, or gets. The only real tension is that this is the third consecutive measurement cycle on a project whose owner keeps naming conversion as the target, but the repair is genuinely time-boxed (the 08-03 read would otherwise be corrupted) and the plan explicitly commits the next cycle to a mechanism-level conversion bet, so approve.

findings.issue: Third consecutive measurement-only cycle (07-16, 07-20, now) on a project whose owner names conversion as the target; a plainly fresh-ground conversion bet was passed over.
findings.evidence: Coverage map (FUNNEL_CHANGELOG.md:108-118) flags the in-app examples/occasion screen (role -> pressed Create) as NEVER attacked, and history says mechanism changes on warm-user steps move this funnel (2026-06-16 win, +14pts) while presentation reshuffles go flat (PR #8). The plan dismisses leak 2 narrowly as 'can't localise the losing sub-step' (PostHog 403), but the project ethos (FUNNEL_CHANGELOG.md:50-57) is ship-unmeasurable-freely. Approve stands only because the instrument repair is time-boxed: it must land before the ~2026-08-03 read accumulates (fix ships 07-22, read is 08-03, so it protects ~12 of the 14 days) or a month of accumulation is lost, and every conversion alternative this cycle would bet on a cause that cannot be verified (403, no in-app replays) - the exact 2026-07-16/last-cycle mistake.
findings.required_fix: None blocking. Owner should note the plan's own commitment (plan.strongest_case_against) that NEXT cycle must produce a mechanism-level conversion bet driven by the repaired read - the never-attacked examples/occasion screen is the leading candidate. A fourth measurement cycle would not be defensible.

findings.issue: The plan surfaces that a documented [FACT] in FUNNEL_CONTEXT is now wrong: claim traffic arrives with code=GOTYOU30 and source=insert|box, not the '?sku only, no code, no source ever arrives' the context asserts.
findings.evidence: FUNNEL_CONTEXT.md:84-86 states as [FACT] the QR link carries only ?sku. Verified in code that claim.html:1187-1188 reads params.get('code')/params.get('source') into state, and api/klaviyo-subscribe.js:76 forwards discount_code to Klaviyo. The plan (tradeoff.unverified_assumptions[0]) reports ~83% of claim start_urls now carry code=GOTYOU30 from session-recording metadata. Correctly raised as an OWNER QUESTION / FACT-correction, NOT used as a lever, and showing a code up front remains owner-rejected - so handling is right.
findings.required_fix: None blocking. Owner should confirm whether GOTYOU30 is a real multi-use printed code (it weakens the 'the discount is the price of the email' premise if so) and resolve the FUNNEL_CONTEXT [FACT]. Do not act on it this cycle.

findings.issue: The fix rests on the 'input' event firing on autofill/paste in mobile webviews; this is spec-correct but browser-dependent and cannot be sized from N=6.
findings.evidence: claim.html:1558-1578 currently binds email_field_engaged to 'focus' only with {once:true}; getVisitorId (claim.html:1165-1179) returns null in the sessionStorage catch. Both defects are confirmed code facts. The 4<6 impossibility (email_field_engaged=4 vs email_entered=6) reproduces in funnel-report for the deploy window. Adding 'input' strictly improves coverage over focus-only even where autofill masks the value, so there is no downside; residual risk is only prevalence, which the plan admits.
findings.required_fix: None blocking. During how_to_verify, actually exercise an autofill/paste-without-focus path and a storage-blocked session, and confirm (a) exactly one email_field_engaged fires via the shared once-flag and (b) all three claim events share one module-scoped in-memory visitor_id, as the plan specifies.
